name: Oxcarbazepine
summary: A prodrug of the sodium-channel blocker MHD (licarbazepine), used for focal seizures with fewer enzyme-inducing drug interactions than carbamazepine.
mechanism: Prodrug rapidly converted to the active metabolite MHD (monohydroxy derivative, licarbazepine), which blocks voltage-gated sodium channels.
targets: Voltage-gated sodium channels (via active metabolite MHD)

pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Parent ~2 h; active metabolite MHD ~9 h
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic reduction to active MHD, then glucuronidation; much weaker enzyme induction than carbamazepine

dosing.adult: Start 300 mg BID, titrate by 300 mg/day weekly; usual maintenance 600–1200 mg/day
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min)

safety.pregnancy: Limited data; possible malformation risk — avoid when possible
warnings: Hyponatremia is common and can be severe — check sodium
SJS/TEN (lower risk than carbamazepine; HLA-B*1502 association)
CNS depression — caution with alcohol and other sedatives
Class warning: suicidal thoughts and behavior
safety.overdose: CNS depression and hyponatremia; supportive care

clinicalPearls: A much gentler enzyme inducer than carbamazepine, but hyponatremia is more common
Cross-hypersensitivity with carbamazepine occurs in ~25% of patients
good: Focal seizures when carbamazepine's enzyme induction is a problem; fewer drug interactions.
bad: Elderly patients (hyponatremia is common) and anyone who cannot tolerate dizziness or diplopia.
